title: Canonical automorphism transport of completed coefficients
statement: Let A be a commutative ring with adic coefficient datum d [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For an isomorphism f:X→Y of schemes, use the equivalence of small pro-etale sites [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. Use the completed coefficient map of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], namely f⁻¹ R_Y→R_X given by the unique map whose composite with every finite quotient projection is the pulled-back projection followed by the canonical constant-ring comparison. It is an isomorphism. Define module transport as the ringed inverse image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] followed by this coefficient identification, and its derived transport as the exact induced functor on complexes localized at quasi-isomorphisms. Restrict it to the completed bounded constructible integral category [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], transporting intrinsic completion, the reduction tower, strata, bounds and compatible etale-origin witnesses. Now fix a prime ℓ, an algebraic closure Ω of Q_ℓ, a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme T on which ℓ is invertible, an automorphism e of T and a finite intermediate extension E of Q_ℓ in Ω [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Use its actual valuation-ring coefficient datum [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], transported by the canonical small field equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-finite-completed-coefficient-map]. Define P_E on the raw rational coefficient category [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] by scalar localization of this additive coefficient-linear integral transport. For E⊆F, use the concrete tensor extension of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. Define the ordinary tensor/transport comparison as the left adjoint mate of the identity-on-sections comparison between scalar restriction followed by e-direct image and e-direct image followed by scalar restriction. Define its derived comparison by compatibility on complexes with the specified derived tensor counits and the exact-transport localization comparisons. Restrict along the faithful integral inclusions, and rationalize using the integral localization comparisons. This defines the specified canonical isomorphism P_F T_{F/E}≅T_{F/E} P_E. Inverse transport is transport along the inverse scheme isomorphism.

proof.text: For pbcIsoCoefficientMap_isIso, apply the already proved completedCoefficient_isIso from CompletedTowerDirectImage. That proof identifies the coefficient map with the projection-normalized profinite constant-coefficient inverse-image isomorphism. Its stronger result applies in particular to a scheme isomorphism.

For pbcIsoModulePullback_isEquivalence, use the map/pullback adjunction on the pro-etale over categories to obtain a continuous site equivalence. The sheaf adjunction unit and the completed coefficient map are invertible. A general module pushforward construction lifts the site equivalence along this ring isomorphism; the normalized module adjunction then makes its left adjoint an equivalence. For pbcIsoModulePullback_eq_completed, use the recorded object and morphism equations of completedAdicChangeData and functor extensionality.

For pbcIsoOrdinaryDerivedComparison_exists, exactness of the module equivalence supplies its mapDerivedCategory as a left-derived pair. Transport the existing ordinary derived pair through pbcIsoModulePullback_eq_completed. The uniqueness isomorphism of left-derived functors has the specified complex-counit equation; naturality along quotientCompQhIso transfers its homotopy-category equation to complexes, and essential surjectivity proves uniqueness.

For pbcIsoCompletedComparison_isIso, use pbcIsoAmbientPullback_preserves to obtain intrinsic completeness of the exact inverse image. The ordinary derived comparison transports this property to the ordinary pullback. The unit-normalized strict-tower comparison pbcActualCompletedPullback_tower identifies completedPullbackComparison with the intrinsic completion-reflector unit. A reflective full-subcategory unit is invertible on a complete object, and the normalized comparison is therefore invertible.

The remaining pbcIsoAmbientPullback_preserves assertion retains its original proof plan: transport the finite reduction tower and its transitions along the exact inverse site equivalence, commute this equivalence with the derived inverse limit used for intrinsic completion, and transport each stratum, common bounded local model and compatible etale origin with its normalization equations. This theorem remains an original named proof obligation.

For pbcIsoIntegralPullback_isEquivalence, use exact ambient full faithfulness. Apply the same preservation theorem to inverse f. The normalized ordinary derived comparisons, derived pullback composition and identity comparisons give J followed by H isomorphic to the identity. They supply an integral preimage of every target object. Full faithfulness and essential surjectivity give the restricted equivalence.

For pbcIsoIntegralPullback_linear, verify preservation of constant scalars after every finite quotient projection. Naturality of the constant inverse-image comparison gives compatibility with the completed coefficient map. Pass to the adjoint ring direct-image map and evaluate its constant-sheaf unit on sections. This makes module direct image A-linear, so its left adjoint is A-linear. Derived functor linearity and faithfulness of the full-subcategory inclusion give the integral assertions.

For pbcIsoScalarRightComparison_exists, first prove naturality of finite scalar extension under the constant inverse-image comparison and conjugate by pbcLevelConstantComparison. The defining completed scalar projection equations and joint monicity give the completed coefficient square. Naturality of the sheaf adjunction unit gives the corresponding direct-image square. On each section, ModuleCat.restrictScalarsCongr identifies the equal composite coefficient actions. Assemble these identity section isomorphisms using PresheafOfModules.isoMk and the fully faithful sheaf forgetful functor. Extensionality and the section normalization prove uniqueness.

For pbcIsoAmbientScalarComparison_exists, first express the specified homotopy left-derived scalar counit as a right Kan extension on cochain complexes; quotient fullness proves its universal property and the quotient comparison identities give its actual complex formula. Precomposition by the exact source transport equivalence and postcomposition by the exact target transport equivalence preserve the right Kan extension. The ordinary complex comparison identifies their targets. The canonical uniqueness isomorphism of right Kan extensions has exactly the displayed counit equation on every complex. Right Kan extension morphism extensionality proves uniqueness. No scalar counit is assumed invertible on arbitrary complexes.

For pbcIsoIntegralScalarComparison_exists, lift the ambient comparison and its inverse componentwise to the full subcategory using ObjectProperty.isoMk. Faithfulness reduces naturality to ambient naturality. The normalization is definitionally the ambient hom, and equality of all ambient components proves uniqueness.

For pbcIsoRationalization, the localization and ScalarLocalization.map have the same object function and send each integral arrow to one tensor its transported arrow; functor extensionality proves equality. For pbcIsoRationalScalarComparison_exists, compose the integral scalar comparison with the two integral/localization comparisons, using associators, to obtain a comparison after precomposing with integral localization. Every localized arrow has a scalar denominator: multiplying by that denominator produces an integral arrow, and the localized scalar identity is invertible. Cancel its image to extend naturality from integral arrows. Every localized object is an integral object, so the prescribed components determine the isomorphism uniquely.
